newsitem.title: CHINA: China says offshore oil output up in first half.
newsitem.headline: China says offshore oil output up in first half.

text.p: China's oilfields in the South China Sea produced 6.78 million tonnes of crude oil during the first half of this year, a 31 percent rise over the same period of 1996, the official Xinhua news agency said on Sunday.
The offshore oilfields are expected to boost crude oil output to 12 million tonnes this year from 11.84 million tonness in 1996.

The oilfields are being exploited under foreign cooperation projects but they come under the jurisdiction of the Eastern South China Sea Company, which is one of the regional companies of the state-run China National Offshore Oil Corporation.
Nine oilfields in the South China Sea have proved to be of commercial value and eight of them have already gone into operation.
Most of China's oil is produced onshore but Beijing is looking to expand offshore output to meet its growing demand for energy.
